p: כָּל הַשּׁוֹנֶה הֲלָכוֹת בְּכָל יוֹם וְכוּלֵּי
Whoever learns halachos every day," etc.
זֶה אֵין לוֹ שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת לְהָעִנְיָן
This has no connection to the subject at hand,
but serves only to conclude with aggadah;
so why did they choose this aggadah?
comes to rectify the first blemish,
they would have been given only
the five books of the Torah
and the book of Yehoshua alone," etc.,
"for in much wisdom is much anger."
That is, on account of the much anger
they needed much wisdom to sweeten it.
Therefore the orders of the Mishnah conclude
they will merit to be purified
from the impurity of the serpent's contamination;
and the Babylonian Talmud concludes with Maseches Niddah,
and we say, "And Maseches Niddah is concluded,"
the impurity of niddah will be removed;
for this came after the sin,
from the curse "I will greatly increase your pain"
and in Midrash Tanchuma at the beginning of Parashas Noach, Tanchuma, Noach 1):
"She sheds her blood and keeps her niddah,
so that she be atoned for the blood that she shed";
that is, that the blemish be rectified
And the Mishnah begins with Berachos,
for through his berachah one recognizes
that everything is from Hashem Yisbarach;
and tefillah, too, is included in berachos.
And it begins with Krias Shema,
which is the acceptance of the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven;
for through the love and the fear,
when he knows that Hashem Yisbarach,
מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
the King of the kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He,
stands over him and sees his deeds,
immediately fear will come to him
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרְמָ"א, אוֹרַח חַיִּים א, א)
and through this will be rectified
the blemish of the serpent's contamination.
גַּם כִּי יִתְנוּ בַגּוֹיִּים עַתָּה אֲקַבְּצֵם וְכוּלֵּי
"'Though they study among the nations, now I will gather them,' etc.:
if they all study, now I will gather them;
and if a few of them,
they will be relieved of the burden of king and princes."
And there they are speaking of talmidei chachamim
so that even the few of them are exempt from taxes.
one who is not able to learn constantly
הוּא גַּם כֵּן בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא
is also a ben Olam HaBa.
This is along the lines of what they said
"'Yet Me they seek day by day,' etc.:
as if he had engaged in it the entire year."
And certainly this does not mean
one who is able to learn more
וְאֵינוֹ לוֹמֵד רַק יוֹם אֶחָד בַּשָּׁנָה
yet learns only one day a year;
רַק דְּמַיְירֵי בְּמִי שֶׁאֵין סִיפּוּק בְּיָדוֹ
rather it speaks of one who is unable,
who was far from the beis midrash,
and could not learn at home,
שֶׁאָז לֹא הָיָה הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה בִּכְתוּבִים
since at that time Torah she'b'al peh was not in writing,
and he had to learn from the mouth of the teacher
so he had to travel three months
to the beis midrash and back,
וְלֹא הָיָה יָכוֹל לִלְמוֹד רַק יוֹם אֶחָד
and could learn only one day;
and about him Rabbi Yochanan expounded
as if he had engaged in it the entire year.
So too here: one who is constrained
הוּא גַּם כֵּן בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא
is also a ben Olam HaBa.
And on this they expounded, as it says,
"The ways of the world are His":
And "do not read" does not mean
to know the ways of Hashem and to walk in them.
Therefore the Talmud concluded with this,
for this too is included in "they study,"
רַק דְּאִי תָּנוּ כֻּלְּהוּ עַתָּה אֲקַבְּצֵם
except that if they all study, "now I will gather them,"
and the entire blemish will be rectified.
And each time we complete it,
we say, "And Maseches Niddah is concluded,"
for the impurity has been removed somewhat,
וְתֵיכֶף אַחַר כָּךְ מַתְחִילִין עוֹד הַפַּעַם
and immediately afterward we begin once again
with Berachos, to accept the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven,
And in the Mishnah as a whole
even though purity leads to holiness
the verse "And he shall purify it and sanctify it."
when he wishes to attain holiness,
But from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
that came from the serpent's contamination,
for when holiness shines upon him,
all matters of impurity are nullified for him,
